candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Numbers
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Numbers, on 14:13-25. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Numbers (c. 365 AD)

On Moses' citation of the divine self-disclosure 'The Lord is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression... by no means clearing the guilty' (Num 14:18), Ephrem reads the formula as the canonical liturgical prayer-of-pardon adopted into the Septuagint Psalter (Ps 86:15, 103:8, 145:8) and extended into every later Christian confession-rite. The verse holds together the two halves of the Name: mercy and justice, neither cancelling the other. Tewahedo penance liturgy (näsḫa-of-näsḫa) cites Num 14:18 as the canonical Old-Testament anchor for the priestly absolution formula; the same formula governs the Lenten qǝne and the Holy Thursday foot-washing.
